correctness.rationale: Rechecked the repaired theorem: triangular Pascal parity gives iid scenery; a fresh conditional coin times a predictable sign gives iid conditional increments of M and the path identity H_k=M_k+2A_{S_k}+1−ω_0 for k≥1. On dyadic N the union-bound tail for short scenery increments is summable; the maximal walk bound with half the threshold accommodates flooring. Uniform o_P(√n) clock replacement and Donsker give the functional limit. The iid scenery LIL gives ±2 on taking m=floor(n/2), and tight centered laws imply escape in opposite directions along environmental subsequences. Independent bounded enumeration (/workspace/branches/8264e53d-70af-482e-a757-266ccb14ee4b/bounded_check.py) checked 510 coefficient prefixes and 10,920 fixed-scenery coin paths through n=6 including decomposition and the bijection; exhaustive moments through n=8 also agreed with the original, now removed variance claim. The enumerations do not establish functional limits.

value.rationale: The natural next question after the known annealed variance-three result is whether fixed environments have a Gaussian fluctuation law, and with what centering. The repair gives an explicit centering, unit variance rate, and shows the uncentered laws are not even tight. The fair setting explains the split without promising a general biased-environment theorem.
